title.narrative: Implementation of the City-to-City Cooperation between Freetown, Sierra Leone, and Zurich, Switzerland, with a focus on urban regeneration

description.narrative:
The City-to-City Cooperation (C2CC) between Freetown and Zurich on the Urban Regeneration of Freetown CBD is an urban development project aimed at revitalizing the city center of Freetown, Sierra Leone. The project is implemented through a partnership between the city of Freetown and the city of Zurich and is designed to improve the physical, social, and economic fabric of the city center, and create new economic and social opportunities for its residents.
In 2019 the cities of Freetown and Zurich, Switzerland, joined forces to establish a City-to-City Cooperation (C2CC) focusing on the urban regeneration of Freetown's Central Business District (CBD) as part of the wider Transform Freetown agenda. Specifically, the C2CC will represent a pilot initiative within the CBD Urban Regeneration Programme (CBDURP).
The objective of the C2CC is to contribute to the overall implementation of the CBDURP, whose overarching statement reads as : “Freetown’s CBD is an economically thriving city centre with employment opportunities for all income levels and offers safe and inclusive public and green spaces for social, cultural and recreational activities for the city’s residents and tourists alike, while at the same time maintaining an ecological environment”.
Two accomplishments (outcomes) are expected from the C2CC initiative: • EA1. An integrated sustainable solution to urban regeneration of the CBD is developed and implemented. • EA2. Knowledge is created and institutional capacity is built at the different levels for urban regeneration.
The C2CC will be implementing the following regeneration measures in the city block surrounding the FCC premises, which is located in the heart of the CBD, namely: · Improving pedestrian areas. · Renewing street lighting. · Introducing a regulated parking system. · Creating more inviting public space. · Landscaping and greening. Integrated with these infrastructural measures, population and stakeholder concerns will be addressed through participatory engagement and safeguarding measures. The C2CC also aims to strengthen the FCC’s technical capacities in the areas of urban regeneration, project management and governance and to create synergies with other ongoing initiatives.
The C2CC will increase the overall safety and amenity of the CBD for the benefit of the whole city population and its visitors by making it more attractive for business and for social, cultural and recreational activities as well as improving its accessibility and environment. The urban regeneration of the CBD can help the city overcome inequality in different ways: - Reducing spatial inequality, through the improvement of infrastructure and services, the upgrading of pedestrian roads, public and green spaces. - Contributing to a more equitable distribution of economic benefits by stimulating economic activity creating job opportunities. - Engaging communities in the planning process through inclusive urban planning ensures that the diverse needs and preferences of the community are considered. - Contributing to a more equitable distribution of environmental benefits by incorporating sustainable and green design principles, such as green spaces, tree planting, and sustainable transportation. More particularly, the project has a strong job creation potential: - The introduction of a regulated parking system will give informal parking attendants potential formal employment opportunities with regular salary, social security (through employment by businesses or self-organised) - The urban regeneration measures through the improvement of street lightning, the establishment of safe pedestrian mobility, and the landscaping and greening will benefit property owners with a potential increase in rental opportunities due to general regeneration, as well as a potential increase of land value. It will also allow for potential increase of commercial activities for businesses and income opportunity due to general upgrade of CBD and increased night time economy.
The project is also aligned with the country’s priorities and approaches for job creation for the youth. The urban regeneration of the CBD will increase its attractivity and potential for tourism, which is aligned with the human development priority sector set by the country, that focuses on job creation focused on tourism and disabilities. Indeed, following the election of the mayor in 2018, FCC developed the ‘Transform Freetown’ agenda for the mayoral term 2019 to 2022. The plan aims to deliver an integrated approach to the city’s development, with inclusivity and innovation at its core. The framework lays out 11 priority sectors in four clusters: resilience (focusing on environmental management, urban planning and housing, and revenue mobilisation); human development (focusing on education, skills development, job creation focused on tourism and disabilities); healthy city (focusing on health, water and sanitation); and urban mobility.
